text:
maria: Ran a full nvprof + Nsight attach on the FP8 enablement run for H100 -> L40S comparison. Noticing periodic token-rate drops around long tails, looks correlated with kernel handoffs and KV cache churn.
raj: Can you paste the flamegraph?
maria: pasted snippet below (trimmed). main hotspot is `te_fp8_gemm` followed by `kv_cache_eviction_worker` and occasional `cudaLaunchKernel` stalls.
```
# flame top entries
te_fp8_gemm            42.3%
kv_cache_eviction_worker 12.1%
cudaLaunchKernel        8.7%
concurrent_batch_merge  6.2%
```
kevin: Hm, `kv_cache_eviction_worker` that high is surprising. What eviction policy are you using? LRU with 0.2 cold threshold?
maria: yes, default L40S profile: `evict_threshold=0.2`, `prefetch_window=128`. I tried bumping to 0.35 in a canary and eviction CPU spikes reduced but tail latency didn't fully go away.
tim: Could be interplay between microbatch jitter and the FP8 kernel workspace allocation. When kernels switch (fast fp8 vs fallback int8), we see short-lived device syncs.
raj: Do we have a trace that shows kernel selection transitions? Maybe the selector is thrashing between `te_fp8_fast` and `te_fp8_safe` for borderline layers.
maria: yeah attached `selector_trace.log` lines:
```
[12:03:01.123] layer:4 select:te_fp8_fast score:0.72
[12:03:01.124] layer:4 select:te_fp8_safe score:0.55 fallback_reason:quant_scale_var
[12:03:01.124] layer:4 select:te_fp8_fast score:0.71
```
kevin: That's thrash. The score delta is tiny. Our hysteresis is 0.1 right now, can we increase it to 0.25 for the rollout?
maria: Did a quick experiment increasing hysteresis to 0.3 — reduced kernel thrash but end-to-end throughput dropped 3% due to more conservative kernel choice.
perf-ci-bot: perf job 2109876600 finished — baseline vs canary: p50 latency +1.8%, p99 +6.1%, tokens/s -2.9%. See link: https://perf.internal/2109876600
raj: p99 up 6% is the killer. We need a path that preserves tail while not falling back to slower kernels often. Any idea why p99 worsened more than mean?
maria: hypothesis: eviction + cold KV cache misses are causing long-tail cuda syncs when a request touches large attention windows and then hits an evicted KV segment. The FP8 kernels amplify this because their workspace allocations force small concurrency windows.
tim: Another angle: transformer-engine's FP8 config `--te-fp8-eager-allocation` defaults to on for L40S. If we turn it off the workspace might be allocated lazily and reduce eviction pressure. Can someone run a quick canary with `--te-fp8-eager-allocation=false`?
kevin: running now on canary-3. Will report.
kevin: quick log: with eager_allocation=false, eviction worker CPU drops ~30%, tokens/s up 1.5%, but nvprof still shows occasional `cudaLaunchKernel` serialization during very long sequences. p99 improved to +2.0% instead of +6.1%.
maria: promising. Could be that eager allocation plus microbatch coalescing caused these device syncs when eviction kicked in.
raj: Long-term fix might be a kernel-aware eviction policy: avoid evicting KV blobs that are hot in the next N requests predicted by the router. We have per-request affinity tags — can we leverage them?
tim: we can piggyback next-request heatmap from the routing layer. Low-effort patch: mark items as "sticky" for 2s when repeated in same connection.
maria: also found an oddity: FP8 calibration scaling (E4M3 vs E5M2) changed the kernel preference for many layers. When we used E5M2 profiles, `te_fp8_fast` was chosen more often but quality delta worsened for some evals.
raj: So there's a tradeoff: E5M2 gains perf but can regress quality for certain attention patterns. We need per-model calibration presets.
kevin: Action items I'm tracking: 1) canary with `eager_allocation=false` (done) 2) increase selector hysteresis to 0.25 for canary-4 3) run routing-affinity sticky prototype 4) add kernel-aware eviction heuristic.
tim: I'll prototype sticky affinity today.
maria: I'll assemble a minimal repro that triggers the thrash and add unit traces (nvtx ranges + `cudaMemInfo` dumps). Putting the repro on gist and linking in this thread.
perf-ci-bot: benchmark 2109876701 queued (will run against hysteresis=0.25).
raj: One more request — add a tiny flag to log when kernel selection flips more than 3 times within a single request: `--kernel-flip-threshold=3`. That will help identify pathological traces in prod.
maria: good idea, will add and roll to canary-4.
kevin: TL;DR: root causes look like a combo of (1) selector hysteresis too low, (2) eager FP8 allocation causing KV eviction pressure, and (3) calibration profile affecting kernel score distribution. Fixes: hysteresis bump, lazy allocation, sticky affinity, kernel-flip logging.
raj: Thanks everyone. If canary-4 shows p99 within 1% of baseline we can stage a wider rollout. :thumbsup:
